newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian call money traded higher on reduced supply.
newsitem.headline: Indian call money traded higher on reduced supply.

text.p: Indian call money was traded higher at 5.5 percent in mid-morning on Tuesday on a slight tightening of liquidity but dealers said rates would stabilise in the 5.0-6.0 percent range for the day.
Call money ended Monday in the 4.75-5.25 percent range.
Dealers said the supply of funds had shrunk as several lenders had invested in treasury bills on tap with the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) and in repos.

"Last week, call was in single digits," said a dealer at a state-run bank. "A good deal of money therefore went into on-tap bill at 4.6 percent and into repos with the RBI at 4.9 percent. There is definitely some tightness in the market today."
He said liquidity would ease later in the week as last Saturday's repos was reversed on February 7.
"Lenders will then either look for higher repos rates or return to lend in the call market if rates are at current levels," he said.
Prices of government securities are expected to fall in reaction to higher call rates.
"Prices will be under pressure as some banks sell securities to raise funds," said a dealer at a state-run bank.
